summary: Choose Plan from the Mode picker in expanded composer Controls (mobile: Agent options) to inspect and discuss changes before implementation. The picker offers Agent, Plan, and Ask.

headings.title: Saving assistant messages for this task

html:
UI Pages Tour

Choose Plan from the Mode picker in expanded composer Controls (mobile: Agent options) to inspect and discuss changes before implementation. The picker offers Agent, Plan, and Ask; Conversation is hidden from it and Settings. A completed plan offers Yes, implement this plan in the same chat, Yes, clear context and implement in a fresh chat, and No, stay in Plan mode to request revisions. Both implementation choices switch to Agent mode. Fresh implementation carries the approved plan and preferences without the planning transcript. Task Contract remains a separate saved preference: planning suppresses compilation and implementation restores it. Permission grants do not permit writes while a task is in Plan.

/agent-ui is the conversational workspace. It exposes conversations, tasks, jobs, waits and attachments from persisted runtime state. Missing authentication values use ordinary ask_user and one normal reply. Literal values remain canonical task data; optional Redaction settings control consumer projections. OAuth authorization retains its protocol-specific interaction.

When an action is processing, its control or panel shows a short status immediately. A small circular indicator appears if it is still pending after two seconds and disappears when the action completes or fails. Reduced-motion mode keeps this indicator still. Closing a dialog dismisses its loading display; it does not cancel an already accepted save or Agent task. Agent execution keeps its own activity and progress display.

The header's Save to SQL button turns green when SQL confirms all data accepted before that click. Large saves can take several minutes; the button keeps checking and stays in its saving state. A temporary connection interruption while checking also keeps checking. Red indicates a rejected or unconfirmed save request, a reported write failure, or a server restart before confirmation; the tooltip explains which occurred. After a write failure, the button continues watching the server's automatic retry and also allows a manual retry. Later changes may need another save; green confirms the data covered by the completed click.

When stopping the server, keep its terminal open until it prints SQL save complete. Safe to close this terminal. Shutdown logs explain when background services are stopping and when SQL saving begins, with elapsed-time updates every five seconds. The final save waits for completion even when it exceeds the normal worker shutdown timeout. Avoid pressing Ctrl+C again or force-killing the server while it is saving. A failed or interrupted save prints a warning instead of claiming completion.

Expand an Agent activity row to inspect the input and output from that exact invocation, projected according to its redaction setting. Completed HTTP requests expose request headers/body, status, response headers/body and available timing/size metadata. Web Search exposes the returned sources; Web Read shows extracted content. Connection rows explain the target, Gateway and authentication state. Expanding a captured Shell row opens its retained and live output stream; collapsing it closes the viewer while the command continues. Running state, exit code and viewer connection state are shown separately. Copy output and Jump to latest operate locally and do not call the model. Python and job operations expose their available execution evidence.

For a Shell command running as a background job, the inspector reads the runtime's retained job status. Output appears when the runtime retains the completed result; the panel explains this while the job is running. Completion freezes elapsed time at the recorded job duration and closes the observer. Missing or incomplete output is labeled explicitly. Opening the inspector does not query the Gateway or restart the job.

Inspection does not pause the Agent. Details become available as each invocation completes, before the task's final answer or Results document. Responses are rendered as data; retrieved HTML cannot execute. Credentials remain literal unless the owning Redaction source is enabled. Hidden reasoning, internal prompts and context-control contents are excluded from this inspector.

The inspector fetches details only when opened. Each section previews at most 64 KiB, with a 256 KiB content budget per invocation; truncation is marked explicitly. Binary content is represented by metadata. Existing HTTP artifact retention is preserved and its metadata remains inspectable. Normal reload/reconnect works while the backend retains the detail. Previews share the trace's in-memory lifetime, with at most 64 per request and 16 MiB across all requests. Evicted details or a server restart show “Execution details are no longer available.” Older Gateways can supply result evidence but cannot retroactively provide transmitted request details.

Use /schedules for the Scheduler Manager (also available from the Agent header calendar icon), /directory for available services, /settings for active configuration, /parameter-editor for Parameter Store profiles, protected values, and reusable agent guidance. Gmail's delivery/sync activity is provider diagnostics, separate from the model decision loop.

Open Settings → Agent behavior → Prompts or /prompt-editor to inspect and edit built-in model instructions. The Prompt Editor includes full and compact wording, default comparison, sample-value previews, and scoped restore actions. Saves apply installation-wide from the next model request.

In Settings, use the magnifying glass (under More on narrow screens) or Ctrl+F / ⌘F to search settings and Gateways. The same search matches labels, setting keys, and help text, and highlights matching text. Escape closes search and restores the full page and your expanded sections.

Settings → Gateways shows one compact table row per Gateway. Use its toggle to turn it on or off, or expand the row for connection details, software updates, and actions. Expanded rows stay open during status refreshes.

The day/night control in each screen's header changes the theme across open tabs in the same browser, including the manual and diagnostic services on the same host. The choice survives reloads. Settings still controls the default theme and automatic appearance mode.

Open /theme or Settings → UI Preferences → Edit themes, colors and conversation background to preview and customize day/night pairs, save favorites, and choose a browser-local conversation image. Apply saves drafts; Restore Default and Favorites save immediately. See Themes and conversation backgrounds for storage scope, reset behavior and recovery.

Linux controllers with integrated management also expose Inference at /inference in desktop/mobile navigation and the directory. Its searchable tabs cover Overview, Instances, Models, Environments & Builds, Hosts & GPUs, Caching, Jobs & Logs, and Preferences. It shares the existing themes and settings editors. See Inference management for setup and the separate Save, Validate and Apply / Restart actions. External-only artifacts omit this surface.

Add to scheduler in a task's bottom action row opens the same scheduling editor as the calendar button beside its prompt. Choose when to run it, or edit its existing schedule. Opening or saving a schedule does not execute the task immediately.

In Parameter Store, the template menu beside New offers Blank, Server, Proxmox Server, Credential, Git Repository, Gmail profiles, and HTTP Connection auth starters. Choose a template and click New to start an unsaved draft. Saving a profile does not enable a skill or connect to its server. The Proxmox guide covers enabling the optional skill and using a saved server profile; Parameter Store explains typed credential privacy and ordinary parameter behavior.

Ordinary chat is sent to the model. Slash commands use application controls and add no model-history turn. Type / to discover the available commands. Command names are case-insensitive. Only /stop (and its /cancel alias) accepts arguments. A command that needs a conversation or run uses the current selection and rejects a stale target.

Command What it requests
/status (/stat) Show the selected conversation's execution, context usage, queue count, token rates and Memory status. Unavailable measurements remain unknown; estimates are labeled.
/new (/newchat, /new-chat) Start a new conversation.
/stop (/cancel) Stop the selected active task, including its preparation phase.
/stop all Stop all currently active tasks across conversations, including preparation and human waits. Does not clear queued work.
/stop <task-number> Stop the task with the displayed number in the open conversation, for example /stop 3. Numbers are assigned at creation and do not change with display or queue order.
/pause Request a pause after the current action when the run allows pausing.
/resume Resume the selected run when its current state permits it.
/compact Request context compaction when available, retaining exact history.
/delete Open the normal confirmation for deleting the selected conversation.
/history Open conversation history.
/settings Open Settings.
/force-reset-reservations Open administrator reservation recovery. If this conversation has one stuck owner, review its force-reset confirmation directly; otherwise select an owner in Reset. Cancelled jobs stay cancelled.
/queue Show queued follow-up work for the selected conversation.
/clearqueue (/clear-queue) Open confirmation to clear queued work that has not started; an empty queue needs no action.
/trace Open the selected run's details, including an older completed attempt.
/help (/commands) Show command help.
/restart Request backend and enabled-Gateway restarts, even during active work. Active work may be interrupted.
/shutdown Shut down the backend and every enabled Gateway, even during active work. Work is saved first; nothing restarts on its own.
/shutdownserver Shut down only the backend after saving its work. Gateways keep running.

/status opens a closeable panel or mobile sheet. It reads saved runtime measurements without asking a model to generate a report. After confirmed deletion, the client opens the nearest older surviving conversation, or New Chat.

Explicit Stop targets use the same native cancellation controls and per-task Save summary preference as the Stop button. A repeated Stop during graceful stopping requests Force stop. Completed, deleted, or replaced attempts are not retargeted; bulk Stop reports any requests it could not deliver. /stop all covers tasks active when the command is submitted, not future tasks or scheduled runs.

Restart first acknowledges the request, then waits for the backend's final save before handing off to the replacement process. Gateway outcomes are reported individually; an unavailable Gateway does not prove that the backend restart failed. A failed final save retains in-memory state for retry. See application commands and restart for the exact ownership and recovery boundaries.

Use the composer and run controls to submit work, attach context, and manage the current run. The task board displays model-authored high-level outcomes, while command cards show actual tool output. Normal chat does not open a browser terminal connection; backend Gateway PTYs remain available to explicit execution capabilities.

Conversation deletion uses one confirmation on desktop and mobile. The controller durably queues deletion and hides the conversation from normal access before background cleanup removes its owned content. A locked cleanup row can remain visible until disk cleanup finishes; active work can delay collection. Acceptance does not mean all saved turns and recovery copies are already gone.

Cleanup discards queued prompts, abandons conversation work and requests cancellation of running operations. Work changing while the confirmation is open does not block the confirmed selection. Already-started external operations may continue; unresolved execution evidence retains its ownership, and independent schedules, monitors and tasks remain. Bulk deletion requires another review if the set of selected conversations changes. See the deletion lifecycle for acceptance, cleanup progress and recovery behavior. While the request is pending, feedback shows Requesting deletion…; the mobile confirmation button shows Queuing…. Close dismisses the desktop dialog without cancelling the submitted deletion. After acceptance, Pending delete, Waiting for save and other cleanup phases describe background work. A notice disappearing does not mean cleanup finished. Failed status reads show Reconnecting and preserve the accepted removal.

Delete task removes the selected logical task and its related history while keeping the conversation and other tasks. It previews the task identity and submits the removal directly. Accepted tasks disappear before their stored payload cleanup finishes. A later history response cannot restore their deleted identities. Task expiry labels show an observed deadline; reaching zero leaves the eligibility decision to the server. See task deletion and cleanup feedback for request, acceptance, cleanup and feedback lifetimes.

Settings → Model routing configures Main and optional Helper. Each role has endpoint, model, context and generation controls, including Provider Default, smTO Recommended and Custom profiles. Expand Generation and context to edit them, then use Save Main or Save Helper. Optional parameters distinguish Provider Default from explicitly configured values. These choices apply to new work; accepted work keeps its captured configuration. The Model Configuration guide explains routing, profile changes and provider compatibility. For ordinary controls elsewhere on the page, see Settings autosave and recovery.

Administrators can open Settings → Operate → Reset to inspect activity-slot owners across accounts. Reservation details show the owning task, request, execution host, resource locks, and available execution evidence. Reclaim stale slots checks retained evidence without stopping healthy work. Kill task & reclaim and Kill all slot owners & reclaim require confirmation of the exact reviewed owners. They fence those tasks against further dispatch and release their server slots immediately, including when a Gateway is unreachable or has no matching operation. The review includes owned child tasks and their reservations. Unrelated queued tasks can then run.

Reset preserves conversations, history, memory, settings, and inference instances. It does not restart services or purge data. Gateway termination is tracked separately: Slots released; remote stop unconfirmed means server capacity is available while remote cleanup still needs attention. Retry remote cleanup checks those operations without restoring their slots. If local task cancellation fails, Retry task cleanup retries only the affected attempts; their server slots remain free and dispatch stays blocked. Stale cleanup continues to require end evidence. Deleting a task or conversation also releases its server reservations and schedules its managed Gateway artifacts for cleanup, retrying when an offline Gateway returns. Artifacts still referenced by another conversation remain available to that conversation; cleanup reports the retained reference and retries when it is removed. The Gateway needs the updated runtime for artifact retirement and restart recovery.

Saved HTTP connections live in Parameter Store, with an HTTP Connection tab for public configuration, credentials, selected-Gateway testing and session disconnect. Settings no longer contains a separate HTTP Connections editor. Metadata, rename, copy reference and delete use the normal Parameter controls; existing profiles appear automatically. See the HTTP guide.

Saving assistant messages for this task

When a complete assistant message has an available task-notebook source, Save to task context keeps that message available for later decisions in the same task. Saving does not start another model request. Saved task context shows the selected messages and their status; View saved message opens the full current text, and Saved · Remove or Remove withdraws the selection. Removal does not delete the original message or retract a request already sent.

Saved for next decision means the selection has not been recorded in a matching submitted input yet. Included in model input records submission, not proof that the model used the message. If context capacity is exceeded, remove selections or use a supported capacity change before continuing. If a source is no longer available under access or retention rules, remove that unavailable selection. The system rereads the original source and reapplies current redaction; saving does not preserve a separate copy of revoked text.

Incomplete or ambiguous messages may have no save action. Failed saves show an error and can be retried; a repeated request does not create duplicate selections. For source matching, retry receipts and the checks before model dispatch, see saved assistant task-context flows.

Directory and navigation groups

Open /directory to find primary pages and the Controller's registered route inventory. Search paths filters the loaded names, paths and descriptions; it does not call those endpoints. An Unavailable primary card means its local route was not present in that inventory. A listed route is not a service health check. API method badges describe the route, and parameter placeholders still need real values when using the API. Ordinary route links do not issue POST actions. Reload Directory to obtain another inventory after the application changes.

Settings, Inference, Manual and Directory group navigation under expandable headings. Activate a heading with a click, Enter or Space to save its collapse choice for the current browser tab. Search can temporarily open matching groups; clearing it restores your choices. A direct link can also reveal its destination without replacing your saved collapse preference. These choices do not change server settings or task behavior.

On narrow screens, Sections opens Settings, Inference or Manual navigation in a dialog. Close it with Close, Escape or an outside click; focus returns to the Sections button when appropriate. Resizing to desktop restores the same navigation panel. Directory keeps its route groups inline. Opening Sections does not reset a collapsed group merely because it contains the current destination.

For the internal data and interaction paths, see Directory and shared navigation flows.

Loading and reconnecting conversations

Desktop chat keeps bounded unsent drafts in the current tab, including their attachment references and temporary options. Reloading can restore the draft; text entered while a conversation is still loading takes precedence over an older cached value. Text longer than 24,000 characters stays in the composer but is not cached. If browser storage is unavailable, a notice explains that recovery may be unavailable. Caching a draft does not submit it as work.

When a submission fails, recovery fills only a still-empty composer that has not been edited since submission. Newer text stays in place. A recovered unsent steering update becomes a normal draft, so review it before sending again.

Desktop and mobile remember the last existing conversation separately from a new draft. Opening New does not erase that return destination. If it has been deleted, the app finds the newest available conversation; a connection failure does not by itself cause the app to forget it. An explicit conversation link opens its named chat.

On desktop, saved messages and current task state load independently. You can see history before conversation settings are ready, but Send remains unavailable until the required settings and target are resolved. Retry settings repairs a failed settings read; a conversation loading error has its own Retry action. An unavailable saved Gateway does not silently redirect work to another target.

An answer to a task's question belongs to that task. While the accepted answer is being processed, Resuming… replaces the old question. If progress refresh fails after acceptance, the page says Response accepted and reconnects; that message does not ask you to submit the same answer again. A later question can have the same wording and still require a new answer.

Live answer text can change or disappear while the response is being validated. Wait for the retained answer and task status before treating a provisional preview as final. A connection warning describes observation; it does not establish that the task or a remote command stopped. Opening history or closing an output viewer also leaves server work running.

Load history opens a run's retained activity. Settings → UI Preferences → Load history on demand is on by default and is shared across devices. Turning it off loads eligible active runs' history after the page's initial reads settle. You can still select Load history yourself. Its progress describes the retained history being scanned; a failed load offers Retry and keeps completed scan work. Collapsing Activity lets an already requested load continue. Navigating to another conversation disposes that view and cancels its pending reads. This control is separate from loading older conversation messages.

Inspect execution opens Evidence for the current operation and any reported blockers; Events shows retained event history. Evidence distinguishes whether a command started, whether its process is running, reported progress and the freshness of the observation. A path mentioned in a command does not by itself confirm that a file was created. Closing the inspector stops that view's observation while server work continues. If an evidence read fails, the previous evidence remains visible with Retry; it may be stale. In Events, use Older activity, Newer activity and Latest activity to browse pages. Show exact event sequence expands grouped progress into individual retained events. Opening an event offers its raw details and any available Tool output or Model output. These output views load when opened and remain separate from the event's JSON.

Older saved turns may offer Load saved task details when their compact record does not contain enough information to restore an interaction. Opening that detail reads retained state and does not rerun the task. See UI ownership for the implementation boundaries and Artifacts, previews and downloads for saved files and their separate preview/download rules.

On mobile, open a response's Message details menu for Files, timing, execution inspection and optional steering/continuation controls. Required questions and approvals stay in the conversation. Closing this sheet preserves the existing controls and their drafts. Reading older messages pauses following; Jump to latest returns to the newest content.

Reading message times

Message clocks use your browser's local timezone and date format. Hover, focus or select a clock to see the full timestamp and relative age; Escape or a click outside closes it. Opening the clock does not open its surrounding activity disclosure or fetch more data. Unknown timestamps are omitted. The first visible reply time stays stable as that reply streams; it is separate from the recorded completion time used for ordering.

Timing labels describe recorded work. Thought includes model request/response generation, while operation timing uses available execution receipts. It is not a measurement of internal reasoning. Parallel work is counted from observed intervals; partial or unavailable measurements stay labeled. See Recorded timing for how durations, overlap and missing receipts are represented.

The timing footer's popup identifies its scope. Total runtime covers the full task lifetime, including queues, pauses and replies; This run excludes earlier replies and gaps between runs. The desktop Worked on this conversation for total adds response durations, including active responses, and excludes time between responses. Concurrent responses can overlap in that sum, so it is not elapsed calendar time. Missing durations or attribution are labeled partial or unmeasured.

Context remaining describes the latest recorded model request, including its reserved output space. Click it to open a copyable diagram of input, generated output, unused output reservation and remaining capacity. Older measurements may be unsplit; unavailable counts and context rejection are labeled explicitly. Component estimates can differ from measured totals. The diagram uses already received data; new messages or tool results can change the next request's budget.

The adjacent tokens read and tokens generated counts accumulate across the task's model calls, including stopped attempts. Average rates use finished calls with matching counts and request durations; they include transport/prefill time and exclude tool/idle time. They are not GPU-only speeds. ≈ marks estimates and — means unavailable. Number animations change presentation only.

Finding loaded content

On desktop, use Find on this screen or Ctrl+F / ⌘F to search the current page. In an open modal dialog, Find stays inside that dialog. Enter selects the next match, Shift+Enter the previous match, and Escape closes Find and restores focus. Matching is literal and case-insensitive, including text across inline formatting. Unsupported browsers keep their normal browser Find shortcut.

Conversation Find covers loaded content only. It can temporarily reveal collapsed text already present on the page, but does not load older messages or fetch unopened output details. Active-runs filtering still applies. Closing Find restores temporary expansion choices; manually changing a disclosure keeps that choice. Queries are not saved. Settings additionally matches its loaded setting metadata and Gateway rows, so a result can match a key absent from visible text.

Workflows

Use the permission and capability editor guide to choose prompt, conversation or global scope, distinguish immediate preset saves from draft edits, and recover from a conflicting save in another client.

Save to workflow beside a user prompt saves its exact text and execution settings, including failed and text-only requests. Unsent drafts can also be saved. Three independent switches optionally copy prior messages, attached inputs and previous tool results. More options → Workflows opens the searchable library with Edit, Run now, Schedule, History and Delete. Runs use fresh Agent reasoning; schedules pin the saved revision. See Workflows.

Reusing earlier prompts

Use Recall previous prompt, or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+H, to browse the newest retained prompts in the desktop composer. Similar prompts appear together, with usage counts and the newest text as the preview. Search also matches older variants inside a group. Open a group, choose the wording you want, then select Use prompt. Enter in the variant list does not insert or submit it. Escape closes Recall and keeps your draft.

Inline completion offers a longer retained prompt after you type at least three non-whitespace characters with the caret at the end. Press Tab or Complete to insert the suggestion, or Escape to dismiss it. A resource picker takes keyboard priority while open. Completing or recalling text does not send it, restore old attachments or change the current permissions and targets. Review the current controls before sending as usual.

Shared history keeps up to 100 distinct text entries; recording an exact repeated prompt moves it to the newest position and increments its usage count. Outer whitespace is trimmed on storage, while internal formatting is retained. See Prompt recall flows for storage, grouping, completion and cancellation sequences.

Immersive composer and instruction resources

Chat opens in the compact immersive view with Debug mode off by default, including on fresh installations. Turn Debug mode on for the full detailed view. Use Settings → UI Preferences → Debug mode by default to change the shared default. Saved choices are preserved.

Continuous prose in compact view is on by default in UI Preferences. It joins consecutive progress narration into flowing paragraphs after each user message. Final answers keep their formatting, and a saved off preference is preserved.

Settings → UI Preferences → Enter action for task replies chooses what Enter does in an active task's reply box: Queue or Steer, with an Interrupt toggle for steering. The default is Steer with Interrupt off, which lets the current response finish before applying the update. Turning Interrupt on interrupts the current response. Queue waits until the preceding task attempt completes successfully and disables the Settings Interrupt toggle. The choice is saved across browser sessions and devices and updates open reply boxes in Standard and Immersive views, including mobile Message details. Each reply box's Interrupt toggle starts from the saved default and follows changes to that default; local toggle choices survive ordinary run updates. Shift+Enter adds a new line. The action buttons still select their named action, and the main composer keeps its existing behavior. Enter continues a finished task; if a submission is uncertain, Enter retries its original action even after the default changes. The instruction editor sequences explain retry identity, pending steering cancellation and the difference between an accepted instruction and confirmed application.

Queue (n) opens the pending continuations in their saved order. You can delete an instruction while it is queued; once scheduling has committed, deletion is no longer available. Failed, stopped or interrupted tasks hold their queued instructions until the task is recovered successfully. The server advances the queue even when the browser is closed, using the preceding attempt's context at dispatch. See Follow-up queues for resource snapshots, retry behavior and the distinction between queued counts and starting children. For an implementation walkthrough of conversation queues, Run After selection and continuation panels, see browser queue flows.

Active runs shows running and waiting work in both Standard and Immersive views. This includes queued or starting runs, timed and scheduled waits, jobs, and waits for resources, input, or approval. Finished, stopped, and paused runs are hidden. Waiting runs keep their status and countdown; completed attempts of an active task remain hidden.

Use the task's arrow or Collapse all tasks / Expand all tasks to shorten or restore Standard view; Immersive view calls these Collapse all chats / Expand all chats. Standard and Immersive retain separate collapse choices. Choices are saved per conversation in this browser and shared by its desktop/mobile tabs. If browser storage is unavailable, choices can still work for the current page. Collapsed tasks retain the full prompt and their reported status. Find can temporarily reveal mounted collapsed text without saving a new collapse choice.

Activity details for this conversation saves the default for prose activity disclosures. Opening one disclosure changes only that view temporarily. A Working... group can later gain narration while preserving its operation rows. A successful group summary reflects the task's final result; expand its details to inspect failed attempts that preceded recovery. Monitoring activity shows recorded process/progress observations and available operation context. An alive or quiet process is not by itself evidence of successful completion.

The Navigator rail on the right marks each active run with a green dot beside its prompt marker. Several markers can have dots at once; the thicker line still marks your reading position. Open the rail to see the same dots beside prompt labels, with the run's status in the tooltip. Compressed markers show a dot if any of their prompts has an active run. These indicators use the same running and waiting states as Active runs and disappear when a run finishes, stops, or pauses.

Auto scroll, below Debug mode, scrolls to the newest message as the conversation continues. To keep the newest activity at the bottom, it moves a task to the bottom when you send a request or follow-up, its reply starts, or its reply finishes. Each task keeps its prompts, follow-ups, replies, and controls together. Streaming tokens and tool progress do not repeatedly reorder tasks. Questions asking for input or approval count as replies. Queued prompts appear immediately and update in place when execution starts; the queue controls still manage scheduling.

The navigator follows this order. Enabling the option or sending a request takes you to the bottom, and incoming replies and updates keep it in view. Changing other View switches, clicking in the conversation, or reordering tasks does not stop it. Scrolling up, opening a task, or navigating to an earlier message pauses automatic following and preserves your reading position; it resumes when you return to the bottom or choose Go to latest. When a task is merged into the message box (Merge prompt), Auto scroll follows that task instead, keeping its newest message, reply, or update just above the box. Turn the option off to restore submission order. It defaults to off, is remembered per conversation in this browser, and is available in Standard and Immersive views and mobile options.

Go to latest appears while you read earlier messages. It returns to the bottom of the conversation, or, when a task is merged into or locked to the message box, to the newest message, reply, or update of that task, keeping it merged. Older saved responses use their recorded completion or last saved time when an exact reply-publication timestamp is unavailable.

Immersive mode keeps the brain toggle immediately before Send on desktop and mobile. It uses the conversation's existing Thinking Default/On/Off setting; an accepted run keeps its captured setting. Type / in the main composer to discover application commands. Help, status, and command results stay available in Immersive mode. /trace asks you to turn on Debug mode to view task details.

Type @ in the main composer, Steer this run, or Continue this conversation to select Gateways, files, saved context, artifacts, or Parameter Store references. This also works inside mobile Message details and with Queue. Enter or Tab selects the highlighted resource without submitting the instruction; Escape dismisses suggestions. Removable chips beside the input show pending attachments and Gateways. Each editor keeps its own selections.

In Continue this conversation, use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to recall user prompts from that task. Up Arrow starts recall on the first line; Down Arrow advances on the last line and restores your unsent draft after the newest entry. Other tasks are excluded, and resource picker navigation keeps priority.

Typing after @ searches across all available categories. Results such as Gateway · workstation-a or Special actions · Use memory can be selected directly. Bare @ keeps category browsing; queries such as @gateway win narrow the search. Resource searches refresh after a 180 ms typing pause, when reopened, and after relevant task or conversation updates. An open search refreshes its cached results after 30 seconds even if the query stays unchanged. Selecting an unavailable resource refreshes the suggestions and preserves your draft.

Saved context and artifacts become available after the conversation exists, with up to 16 context sources selected. Search shows metadata; selecting a result checks that it is still available. Parameter results show names and field names, excluding stored values. Selecting a parameter inserts its @ reference for validation when you send. Opening Upload file removes the @file query even if you cancel the file chooser. For the internal search, selection and ownership sequences, see Composer resource flows.

Memory tools are always available for explicit reads and writes. Automatic lookup, injection, guidance, checks and proactive learning are off by default. Choose @ → Special actions → Use memory, or type @memory and select Use memory, to insert @use_memory and enable automatic support for that task and its continuations. Remove the token before sending to leave automatic support off. Each new task requires its own opt-in for automatic support; explicit memory requests need no token.

A selected Gateway is added to the addressed run's available targets when the instruction is applied. Its primary Gateway, existing working directories, and permissions are preserved. Steering applies resources at the next safe processing boundary; Steer without interrupting waits for the current response. Continuations and queued continuations apply resources before the child's first model step.

Explicit parameter references are captured when the instruction is accepted. Retrying an instruction or dispatching its queued continuation uses that captured value even if the Parameter Store changes. New explicit references replace matching saved bindings; unmentioned bindings carry forward. An unresolved parameter reference can prevent acceptance and must be resolved before inference; quoted code references and email addresses remain literal text. Validation errors retain your draft and selections. Cancelling a pending instruction applies none of its resource changes.

Memory Editor

Open Settings → Agent behavior → Memories or /memory-editor to browse, create, clarify, and delete saved memories. The Memory Editor shares the Prompt Editor layout, supports general and project scope, and protects unsaved drafts and concurrent edits.
